name: The Most Precious Blood of Our Lord
history: A feast honouring the Blood of Christ, shed for our redemption at the circumcision, in Gethsemane, at the scourging and on the cross, and given to us in the chalice. Pius IX extended it to the whole Church in 1849. Though now joined in the newer calendar to Corpus Christi, July is still kept as the month of the Precious Blood.
life: Devotion to the Precious Blood runs through the Church’s history, from Saint Peter’s words that we were ransomed not with silver or gold but with the precious blood of Christ, to the mystics of the Middle Ages. In the nineteenth century it was spread by Saint Gaspar del Bufalo, who founded the Missionaries of the Precious Blood in 1815. In 1849 Pius IX, in exile at Gaeta during the revolution in Rome, was urged by one of Gaspar’s missionaries to promise the feast to the whole Church, and after his return he did so. Pius XI raised its rank in 1934, the nineteenth centenary of the Redemption, and John XXIII approved a litany of the Precious Blood in 1960. The 1969 calendar joined the feast to that of the Body and Blood of Christ, but the devotion remains, and the traditional calendar keeps it on 1 July.
prayerTo: Lord Jesus Christ, You shed Your Precious Blood for me in the garden, at the pillar and on the cross, and You give it to me in the chalice. Wash me clean of my sins, make me grateful for so great a price, and let Your Blood plead for the whole world before the Father. Amen.
penance: Pray the Stations of the Cross or the Sorrowful Mysteries today, and if you can, receive Holy Communion with special thanksgiving.
meditation: You were bought with a price. Look at a crucifix today and ask what you are worth to Him.
prayer: Almighty, eternal God, Who made Your only-begotten Son the Redeemer of the world, and willed to be reconciled by His Blood, grant us, we beseech You, so to worship in this sacred rite the price of our salvation, and to be so protected by its power against the evils of the present life on earth, that we may enjoy its everlasting fruit in heaven. Through the same Christ our Lord…
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
